title: Petra and the Portrait
premise: Elodie Kavanagh, a pest controller who treats infestations like arithmetic, is hired to clear a decaying manor where the previous exterminator vanished. The 'pest' turns out to be a portrait in the attic that paints its subjects one brushstroke ahead of their lives, and every mirror in the house begins lagging reality by exactly one second — long enough for something to slip through. Elodie discovers the house's last heir, Marguerite, survived decades inside the portrait's song by refusing to sing its final verse, which grants the painter complete ownership of whoever finishes it. In the climax, Elodie must choose between burning the portrait and losing their own reflection forever, or learning the verse to trap the painter at the cost of becoming his next canvas; they sing it wrong on purpose, corrupting the frost pattern, and walk out half-painted but free.
about_author: Juniper Nakamura is a former conservator of historic homes who spent years cataloguing the strange things owners refuse to discuss. She writes horror from a farmhouse whose mirrors she has never once hung facing each other.

chapters.title: The Contract Clause
chapters.summary: Elodie Kavanagh takes a job at Hollowmere Manor: something is leaving greasy fingerprints at ceiling height, and the fee is triple her usual rate. POV Elodie. The beat is wary competence — she counts doors, checks traps, and notes the client, Marguerite Voss, never blinks.

chapters.title: Fingerprints at Ceiling Height
chapters.summary: Elodie surveys the manor and finds prints ascending the staircase wall, five-fingered but too wide, spaced like someone walking on air. POV Elodie. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into the first honest fear she's felt in years.

chapters.title: Marguerite Keeps the Lights On
chapters.summary: The elderly Marguerite explains her rules: forty-one bulbs, all burning, doors counted aloud each night. She hasn't slept lying down since 1974. POV Elodie. Beat: pity warring with suspicion as Elodie realizes the rules are precise, practiced, and terrified.

chapters.title: What the Traps Catch
chapters.summary: Overnight, Elodie's glue boards catch nothing animal — instead they hold flakes of dried paint arranged in a spiral. POV Elodie. Beat: the pest controller's worldview cracks; this is not an infestation, it's an invitation.

chapters.title: The Attic Portrait
chapters.summary: Following the paint trail, Elodie finds a life-sized portrait of a faceless man in a room where dust refuses to settle. His hand holds a brush still wet. POV Elodie. Beat: awe and violation — being looked at by something with no eyes.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Every mirror in the manor begins reflecting rooms one second behind. Elodie watches their own reflection raise a hand they haven't raised yet. POV Elodie. Beat: vertigo; the house is no longer describing reality, it's drafting it.

chapters.title: The Song From the Walls
chapters.summary: A lullaby seeps through the plaster at dusk, sung in two voices — one of them Marguerite's, though she sits silent beside Elodie. POV alternating Elodie/Marguerite. Beat: the horror of hearing your own voice used without permission.

chapters.title: Verse One, Verse Two
chapters.summary: Marguerite confesses: the song has three verses. Sing the first and you dream true; the second and you lose your shadow. She has hummed around the third for fifty years. POV Marguerite flashback. Beat: loyalty — she stayed to keep the thing fed and contained.

chapters.title: The Previous Exterminator
chapters.summary: Elodie finds Tomas Reyes's van rusting in the carriage house, his ledger detailing how he tried to burn the portrait and failed. His final entry: 'It learns your hands.' POV Elodie. Beat: dread of inheritance — she is following a script already written.

chapters.title: Brushstrokes Ahead
chapters.summary: The portrait now shows a figure resembling Elodie, mid-stride, painted slightly ahead of wherever she actually stands. When she stops, it waits. POV Elodie. Beat: hunted feeling; her future is being composed without her consent.

chapters.title: Doors Miscounted
chapters.summary: The nightly count comes up forty-three doors in a thirty-eight-door house. Two extra doors are painted shut; one breathes. POV Elodie. Beat: the collapse of order — her arithmetic, her armor, no longer balances.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marguerite reveals she was the painter's model in 1974; he keeps her young-ish, unaging, as long as she never finishes the song. Her loyalty to him vs. the truth of what he is. POV Marguerite. Beat: complicity exposed — she isn't just a victim; she's staff.

chapters.title: The Frost Writes First
chapters.summary: Frost blooms across every window in identical patterns: musical notation. The house is transcribing the third verse where anyone can read it. POV Elodie. Beat: urgency — the song wants to be finished and is doing the work itself.

chapters.title: Reflections With Opinions
chapters.summary: The lagging reflections begin diverging — Elodie's mirror-self mouths warnings, then pleas, then instructions. POV Elodie. Beat: uncanny alliance; the only ally in the house is her own delayed image.

chapters.title: Tomas, Still Here
chapters.summary: Inside a mirror's one-second gap, Elodie glimpses Reyes, half-painted, living in the lag. He tells her the verse must be sung wrong — off-key, backwards — to poison the pattern. POV Elodie. Beat: desperate hope with a terrible price tag.

chapters.title: Power Corrupts the Brush
chapters.summary: The painter offers Elodie a deal through the portrait: finish the verse willingly and gain his power — command over reflection, time, form. He shows her Marguerite's stolen decades as proof. POV Elodie. Beat: temptation rendered genuinely attractive.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite begs Elodie to take the deal and free her, revealing she lured Reyes here as a sacrifice when he refused. POV Marguerite. Beat: shame and self-justification colliding; truth finally outweighs fifty years of loyalty.

chapters.title: Counting Down the Doors
chapters.summary: The house begins deleting doors; the exits shrink to one. Frost notation covers the floors. The portrait's Elodie is nearly complete — missing only her mouth. POV Elodie. Beat: claustrophobic sprint toward the choice.

chapters.title: The Third Verse
chapters.summary: Cornered in the attic, Elodie reads the frost and opens her mouth. The painter leans out of the canvas to listen. POV Elodie. Beat: held breath — the climactic moment before the note lands.

chapters.title: Sung Wrong, On Purpose
chapters.summary: Elodie sings the verse backwards and flat, feeding the corruption into the frost pattern. The portrait screams in drying paint; the mirrors snap into real-time; Reyes's lag collapses. POV Elodie. Beat: triumphant defiance at personal cost.

chapters.title: Half-Painted
chapters.summary: Dawn: Elodie's left side remains faintly pigmented, her reflection a half-second slow forever. Marguerite, freed, ages sixty years in an hour and dies content. POV Elodie. Beat: grief braided with release.

chapters.title: The Next Contract
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Elodie takes a new job — a farmhouse with fingerprints on the ceiling. In her van's mirror, her reflection smiles first. POV Elodie. Beat: quiet, unresolved dread; some songs survive a wrong verse.
